_doc: The law book (Systems/Laws.cs): the council sets the punishment for each crime the watch catches heroes at. Each sentence carried out moves order (unrest, negative calms it), fear (a share of would-be offenders who think twice), the guilds' standing and the temple god's favour, and the offender's loyalty. fine multiplies the usual fine. The default is the old fine, so a town that never opens the book plays as before.

crimes.name: Brawling
crimes.text: Wrecking a taproom, breaking a drover's jaw, starting what the watch has to finish.

crimes.name: Theft
crimes.text: A hand in a shop's till, a purse lifted at the market.

punishments.name: A fine
punishments.text: The magistrate fines them and lets them go. Nobody minds much either way.
punishments.sentenced: and the magistrate fines them {fine} gold

punishments.name: The stocks
punishments.text: A day in the stocks on the square, pelted with cabbage. The shopkeepers like it; the priests think it petty.
punishments.sentenced: and they spend a day in the stocks on the square while the market throws cabbages

punishments.name: Flogging
punishments.text: Ten lashes at the gate. Few dare the same crime twice, but the temple preaches against it and heroes remember.
punishments.sentenced: and they take ten lashes at the gate, with half the town watching

punishments.name: Temple penance
punishments.text: A week scrubbing the temple steps and a vigil at the altar. The temple is pleased; the guilds call it soft.
punishments.sentenced: and they are sent to scrub the temple steps for a week and keep vigil at the altar

punishments.name: Restitution
punishments.text: Twice the harm paid back. The guilds call it justice; it empties a hero's purse.
punishments.sentenced: and the magistrate makes them pay back twice over, {fine} gold

trial._doc: Every catch goes before the court, with no dice: 10 + the Captain of the Watch's Investigation (the watch's own if the seat is empty), +1 for each watchPer watchmen up to watchMost, + witnesses for a crime done before a crowd, against 10 + the accused's Deception. Ties go to the court. A guilty one who walks free costs acquitted Mandate. Once the town reaches a truth spell's tier and a hero at home can cast it, the council may order trials held under it; each pays the caster fee gold. certain means no lie holds; bonus adds to the evidence instead.

truth.text: A mage reads the accused's surface thoughts for the court: the case gets much stronger.
A priest or bard holds the trial in a circle where no one can lie: the guilty are always found so.

trial.freed: . They swear they did nothing, and the court can't prove otherwise (evidence {evidence} against their tale {lies}): they walk free
trial.under: . Held under {magic}, the trial is short

changed: The council writes it into the law book: {crime} is now punished by {punishment}.
